intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia (HSSD) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SLC13A1 gene, which encodes the renal sodium-sulfate cotransporter NaS1, on chromosome 7q31.

checks.claim: Hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia (HSSD) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the SLC13A1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Through the use of exome or genome sequencing and GeneMatcher (https://genematcher.org), 5 children from 4 families with biallelic variants in SLC13A1 and a skeletal dysplasia phenotype were identified.
checks.explanation: The probands include homozygous cases (probands 2 and 5) and compound heterozygous cases (probands 1, 3 and 4), and the paper links these variants to hyposulfatemia and skeletal phenotypes. The name 'HSSD' does not appear in the paper.

checks.claim: The SLC13A1 gene encodes the renal sodium-sulfate cotransporter NaS1.
checks.evidence_quote: This requires the SLC13A1 (Solute Carrier Family 13 Member 1) encoded Na+‐sulfate cotransporter (NaS1) in the (apical) brush‐border membrane
checks.explanation: The paper states that SLC13A1 encodes the renal Na+-sulfate cotransporter NaS1.

checks.claim: The SLC13A1 gene is located on chromosome 7q31.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient had a 20 Mb region‐of‐homozygosity on chromosome 7q31.32 containing both the SLC13A1 and the CFTR gene
checks.explanation: The paper places SLC13A1 within 7q31.32.

paragraphs.text: Hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia is an autosomal recessive disorder in which loss of function of the renal sodium-sulfate cotransporter NaS1 (SLC13A1) leads to renal sulfate wasting and low plasma sulfate levels. Affected individuals have a skeletal dysplasia, thought to reflect reduced availability of sulfate for sulfation of cartilage proteoglycans.

checks.claim: Hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient had a 20 Mb region‐of‐homozygosity on chromosome 7q31.32 containing both the SLC13A1 and the CFTR gene, while his parents were heterozygous for both variants
checks.explanation: An affected homozygous child born to heterozygous carrier parents fits autosomal recessive inheritance. The title also describes the variants as biallelic.

checks.claim: In hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia, loss of function of the renal sodium-sulfate cotransporter NaS1 (SLC13A1) leads to renal sulfate wasting.
checks.evidence_quote: We found profound hyposulfatemia due to complete loss of renal sulfate reabsorption.
checks.explanation: The paper attributes the patient's low sulfate to complete loss of renal sulfate reabsorption.

checks.claim: In hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia, loss of NaS1 function leads to low plasma sulfate levels.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that loss of the SLC13A1 gene leads to profound hypersulfaturia and hyposulfatemia
checks.explanation: The paper concludes that SLC13A1 loss causes low plasma sulfate.

checks.claim: Individuals with hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia have a skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: The main clinical features were enlargement of joints and spondylo-epi-metaphyseal radiological abnormalities in early childhood, which improved with age.
checks.explanation: The patient had a skeletal dysplasia.

checks.claim: The skeletal dysplasia in hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia is thought to reflect reduced availability of sulfate for sulfation of cartilage proteoglycans.
checks.evidence_quote: implies that chondrocytes mainly rely on inorganic sulfate from the extracellular space. Significantly reduced chondroitin 4‐sulfate was also observed in the cartilage of SLC13A1‐deficient Texel sheep.
checks.explanation: The paper discusses this mechanism, but in the patient urinary chondroitin sulfation was not reduced, so the paper could not confirm it.

paragraphs.text: The biochemical hallmark of the disorder is a markedly reduced plasma or serum sulfate concentration with inappropriately high urinary fractional excretion of sulfate, consistent with impaired renal tubular reabsorption of sulfate.

checks.claim: The biochemical hallmark of hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia is a markedly reduced plasma or serum sulfate concentration.
checks.evidence_quote: as well as an over 80% reduction in plasma sulfate levels
checks.explanation: The paper reports plasma sulfate reduced by more than 80% in the patient.

checks.claim: Individuals with hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia have inappropriately high urinary fractional excretion of sulfate.
checks.evidence_quote: Reference values for Fractional Sulfate Excretion (FEsulfate) range from 13% to 34%, whereas the patient's FEsulfate was close to 100%
checks.explanation: The patient's fractional sulfate excretion was close to 100%, against a reference range of 13–34%.

checks.claim: The low plasma sulfate and high urinary fractional excretion of sulfate in hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia are consistent with impaired renal tubular reabsorption of sulfate.
checks.evidence_quote: We found an FEsulfate close to 100%, consistent with complete loss of renal sulfate reabsorption in our patient, as well as an over 80% reduction in plasma sulfate levels.
checks.explanation: The paper explicitly interprets these findings as loss of renal sulfate reabsorption.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance, affected individuals carrying biallelic SLC13A1 mutations.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: The patient was the only child of non‐consanguineous healthy Dutch parents with normal heights.
checks.explanation: Healthy heterozygous parents of a homozygous affected child fit recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Individuals affected with hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia carry biallelic SLC13A1 mutations.
checks.evidence_quote: A homozygous g.122839967G>A (Chr7[GRCh37]), c.34C>T, p.(Arg12Ter) variant was identified in the first exon of the SLC13A1 gene
checks.explanation: The only affected individual carried biallelic (homozygous) SLC13A1 variants.

paragraphs.text: Tise et al. (2016) found that heterozygous nonsense variants in SLC13A1, identified in a population cohort, were associated with decreased serum sulfate concentrations, supporting the role of NaS1 in determining circulating sulfate levels in humans.

checks.claim: Tise et al. identified heterozygous nonsense variants in SLC13A1 in a population cohort.
checks.explanation: This 2025 paper mentions the earlier heterozygous nonsense variants only as background. It does not say they came from a population cohort or that they were found by this group.

checks.claim: Tise et al. found that heterozygous nonsense variants in SLC13A1 were associated with decreased serum sulfate concentrations.
checks.evidence_quote: 2 rare, unlinked, heterozygous nonsense variants in the corresponding gene, SLC13A1, NM_022444.4:c.34C>T p.(Arg12∗) and NM_022444.4:c.144G>A p.(Trp48∗), have previously been associated with a 27% reduction in serum sulfate levels (0.25 vs 0.36 mM in controls)
checks.explanation: The association is described as an earlier finding, not a result of this paper. The 2016 study the draft cites is not identified as Tise et al. here.

checks.claim: The association of heterozygous SLC13A1 nonsense variants with decreased serum sulfate supports a role of NaS1 in determining circulating sulfate levels in humans.
checks.evidence_quote: Consistent with the critical role of SLC13A1 in sulfate homeostasis, 2 rare, unlinked, heterozygous nonsense variants in the corresponding gene
checks.explanation: The paper presents the association as consistent with SLC13A1's role in sulfate homeostasis.

paragraphs.text: In individuals with hyposulfatemia and skeletal dysplasia, homozygous or compound heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the SLC13A1 gene were identified by exome sequencing; functional studies showed reduced sulfate transport by the mutant NaS1 proteins.

checks.claim: Homozygous or compound heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the SLC13A1 gene were identified in individuals with hyposulfatemia and skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: Through the use of exome or genome sequencing and GeneMatcher (https://genematcher.org), 5 children from 4 families with biallelic variants in SLC13A1 and a skeletal dysplasia phenotype were identified.
checks.explanation: Both homozygous and compound heterozygous loss-of-function variants were found.

checks.claim: The SLC13A1 mutations in individuals with hyposulfatemia and skeletal dysplasia were identified by exome sequencing.
checks.evidence_quote: The homozygous (Arg12Ter) variant in SLC13A1 was found by exome sequencing performed in a patient with unexplained skeletal dysplasia.
checks.explanation: The variant was found by exome sequencing.

checks.claim: Functional studies showed reduced sulfate transport by the mutant NaS1 proteins encoded by SLC13A1 mutations found in individuals with hyposulfatemia and skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: This variant causes a gain of stop predicted to result in a truncated protein and has previously been shown to cause total loss‐of‐function in Xenopus laevis oocytes.
checks.explanation: This paper did no functional studies itself. It cites an earlier oocyte study that showed total loss of function for this single variant.

paragraphs.text: Mice deficient in Slc13a1 (Nas1-null mice) showed hyposulfatemia due to increased urinary sulfate excretion, along with reduced growth, providing a model for the human disorder.

checks.claim: Slc13a1-deficient (Nas1-null) mice showed hyposulfatemia.
checks.evidence_quote: An existing SLC13A1 knockout mouse model showed similarly reduced plasma sulfate levels and hypersulfaturia
checks.explanation: The paper reports reduced plasma sulfate in the knockout mice.

checks.claim: The hyposulfatemia in Nas1-null mice was due to increased urinary sulfate excretion.
checks.evidence_quote: An existing SLC13A1 knockout mouse model showed similarly reduced plasma sulfate levels and hypersulfaturia
checks.explanation: The mice had low plasma sulfate together with hypersulfaturia.

checks.claim: Nas1-null mice showed reduced growth.
checks.evidence_quote: The SLC13A1−/− mouse shows general growth retardation but no gross histological bone abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The paper states the knockout mice show general growth retardation.

checks.claim: Nas1-null mice provide a model for human hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia.
checks.evidence_quote: The SLC13A1−/− mouse shows general growth retardation but no gross histological bone abnormalities.
checks.explanation: The mouse matches the patient's biochemistry, but the paper notes it has no gross bone abnormalities. It does not explicitly call it a model of the human disorder.
